issues.detail: The Greek 'μη ξενιζεσθε' means 'do not be amazed/surprised' (don't treat it as a strange thing). The Vietnamese 'chớ lấy làm lạ' is a reasonable rendering, but the phrase 'để thử nghiệm' (to test/for testing) is an addition/mistranslation of the purpose. The Greek 'προς πειρασμον' describes the *nature* of the fire (it is a fire *of* trial/testing), not a purpose for which the fire is happening. More importantly, the Vietnamese adds 'để thử nghiệm' as a secondary action, whereas the Greek identifies the fire itself as a 'fire of trial'.
